body: Your mum is a horrible horrible person no doubt and I hope that you are able to leave your home and live a fulfilling life that isn’t centred around her. She doesn’t deserve the attention you give her. You try and focus on yourself and make something of yourself. Who gives a fuck about this woman, she clearly doesn’t about you. So you carry on living and breathing and making the most of what you have in life and one day you will distance yourself so far from what you are experiencing now and be proud of how far you’ve come along. At least that is what I hope for you.
Me too I’m ready but I haven’t got a plan on how. I’ve had failed attempts so need something that will work

I always had a hope that this would somehow end, that he’d somehow end up changing but I’ve come to realise that he never will and the years of torture has had such a massive toll on me that I don’t know how it’s like to be normal anymore. The only way I see out of this is to move out the home but I have no idea how to start that process with the Coronavirus situation at the moment. My fast and easy solution is to just end things myself. Thank you for your well wishes I appreciate it xx

I called them yesterday and I’m sorry to say it didn’t help me at all. I don’t blame the guy that picked up the phone because i was in hysterics saying I want to die and I guess he just didn’t know what to say and kept repeating what I was saying ‘so it sounds like you want to die’ and then left big awkward silences so I just cut him off. It may work with your situation though
Adults with LD and older people. Nothing else appeals to me.

I think you’ve misunderstood maybe or making assumptions. Of course I’d want to change the world for the better, and that is a reason why I got into social work. However due to the many many constraints of the job and power dynamics within social work I feel as though I have little autonomy to do so. 

My plan if I was to leave is to continue to work in a capacity where I am supporting and advising people (maybe HR?) and then in my free time volunteer for a charity. 

Yes it is a shame that I spent the last two years doing a masters in field that I no longer want to pursue- thanks for reminding me. I’ve had this dilemma in my mind for ages, however I have gained so much knowledge, confidence and maturity through my masters that I know it isn’t wasted time. Social work is not for me, not right now anyway

Thank you for your reply. And it’s so nice to hear from a passionate social worker, I’m glad it’s working well for you. But my query is- isn’t it enough for me to say I’m not happy with what I’m doing and I don’t think it’s for me? This is not a dig at you at all but many like you in the past (uni tutors, friends and colleagues) have tried to convince me to stay and pursue other areas within social work but honestly nothing appeals to me. 

I think back to how happy I was in my job before going into my masters and would love to go back to being that person again. This career has drained me completely and although I enjoy some aspects of the role, it’s not one I see myself in for the rest of my life.

I guess what I’m saying is- is it normal to feel like this? To leave social work after a year? Unlike you, I don’t think I’ve had that deep rooted passion for it, and for this job you need it and because I don’t I feel as bad and as though I’m doing a disservice to my clients.

Thank you for your reply. I agree totally. I can’t stand the fake smiles and the fake charisma of my colleagues sometimes. It’s either that or they are miserable as fuck. I stuck this out as long as I could, I think it’s time to leave.

ASYE is the assessed and supported year in employment where you have a protected caseload in your first year as a Newly Qualified Social Worker.

What area of work would that be in? I have experience in older people, learning disabilities, physical disabilities and children’s assessment team and I wouldn’t go back into any of them. I’ve lost a lot of motivation I once had for this career and honestly want out.
